summary: In 1911 a fire at the Triangle Waist Company factory in Manhattan killed 146 mostly immigrant young women, trapped by locked doors and a failed fire escape; owners Max Blanck and Isaac Harris, who had crushed a strike and profited from insurance fires, were acquitted.

evidence.note: 1881 assassination of Alexander II and the pogroms that drove the Jewish emigration
1903 Kishinev pogrom in Bessarabia described in detail
Blanck and Harris, born in Russia, flee pogroms and reach New York by the early 1890s
Triangle Waist Company founded 1900, factory in the Asch Building from 1902
1909 garment strike led by Clara Lemlich; owners use police, gangsters and a fake union
brokers' collusion and the owners' repeated suspicious insurance fires
the March 1911 fire itself, locked door, elevator and fire escape collapse, 146 dead
manslaughter trial and acquittal in December 1911
1913-1914 violations and fines; company finally closed in 1918

notes: Primary subject is the event, so roles are empty; Blanck and Harris are listed as one secondary group. The covered span starts at the 1881 pogroms because they are tied to the owners' own emigration; if treated as pure background, start would be about 1890. Scope set to local (New York City) although the Russian Empire background adds RU and MD to the setting. Frances Perkins and OSHA legacy is brief, so reaches_present is false.
